title: A 24-Gd nanocapsule with a large magnetocaloric effect

synthesis.procedure: Prepared solvothermally at 160 °C from isonicotinic acid, CuO and Gd(NO3)3·6H2O in a 5:3:6 molar ratio. The article identifies DMF as the source of in situ-generated DMC and carbonate anions but does not give a solvent quantity or reaction duration in the main text.

properties.summary: Weak antiferromagnetic interactions were inferred from temperature-dependent susceptibility. The cluster exhibits a large magnetocaloric effect, with the largest reported magnetic entropy change among the molecular clusters compared in the article.

measurements.name: maximum −ΔSm
measurements.conditions: approximately 2.5 K; magnetic-field change ΔH = 7 T

source_locations.location: cluster definitions and structural discussion; Figs. 1–2

magnetic susceptibility and magnetocaloric discussions; Fig. 3

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The Gd24 cluster is a closed capsule assembled from symmetry-related Gd12 units. Its polyhedral backbone is described as three Gd6 hexagonal rings capped by two Gd3 triangles, with carbonate and bridging water connecting the Gd centers; DMC anions cover and stabilize the capsule.

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by the reported solvothermal method at 160 °C using isonicotinic acid, CuO and Dy(NO3)3·6H2O in a 5:3:6 molar ratio. The article identifies DMF as the source of in situ-generated DMC and carbonate anions but does not give a solvent quantity or reaction duration in the main text.

properties.summary: The cluster shows a smaller magnetocaloric effect than Gd24. Frequency-dependent out-of-phase ac susceptibility indicates slow magnetic relaxation and weak single-molecule-magnet behavior, although no χ″ peak was observed even up to 9111 Hz.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The Dy24 compound is reported as an isomorphous, discrete capsule-like analogue of Gd24. Its two lattice water molecules are located within the capsule cavity.
